usdRate.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, exchange rates by currency (US dollar central rate), 30 October 2026
usdRate.note: Central rate N1,345.7565 per US dollar (buying 1,345.2565, selling 1,346.2565); World Bank 2025 average 1,518.4.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: National Bureau of Statistics CPI, September 2026, via Voice of Nigeria
inflation_cpi.note: Headline inflation 14.63% year on year in September 2026 (15.39% in August; 20.98% in September 2025); food inflation 19.59%. NBS report released 15 October 2026, read through the state broadcaster.

inflation_projection.sourceName: NBS CPI via Voice of Nigeria (14.63% in September 2026); World Bank CPI inflation 2021-2025
inflation_projection.note: Inflation ran between about 15% and 33% a year over 2021-2025 (23.0% in 2025) and has fallen to 14.6%, while the central bank's 6-9% target band (as listed by the BCEAO, September 2026) has not been reached in recent years, so 14% is used for long-range plans.

policy_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, key decisions of the Monetary Policy Committee, 21-22 September 2026
policy_rate.note: MPR reset to 23% from 26.5% at the 307th MPC meeting; standing facilities corridor +50/-300 basis points around the MPR.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026 (savings deposit rate)
savings_account_rate.note: Average savings deposit rate 5.36% in September 2026 (7.46% in August).

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026 (3-month deposit rate)
fdr_3m_rate.note: Average 3-month deposit rate 10.33% in September 2026 (10.34% in August).

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026 (12-month deposit rate)
fdr_1y_rate.note: Average 12-month deposit rate 10.50% in September 2026 (10.30% in August).

dps_rate.note: No monthly recurring deposit product with a published rate was found in Central Bank of Nigeria statistics.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: World Bank WDI, deposit interest rate (FR.INR.DPST), Nigeria
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: 11.27% average for 2025; CBN monthly averages by term in September 2026 were 5.36% (savings) to 12.20% (1 month).

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.sourceName: Debt Management Office, FGN Savings Bond offer for subscription, October 2026 (3-year bond due 14 October 2029)
sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Retail FGN Savings Bonds are offered monthly from N5,000 (maximum N50 million) with quarterly interest: 14.071% for 3 years and 13.071% for 2 years in the October 2026 offer (opened 5 October, settled 14 October). No 5-year tenor is offered, so the 3-year rate is used.

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, government securities: Nigerian Treasury Bills primary auction of 28 October 2026 (91 days)
tbill_91d_rate.note: Stop (discount) rate 15.40% on the 91-day bill, about a 16.0% yield; the 364-day bill stopped at 15.80% (about 18.8% yield).

tbond_5y_rate.note: No FGN bond with about 5 years to maturity was auctioned in 2026 that could be read: DMO auctions from July to October 2026 offered only 2034-2038 maturities.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Debt Management Office, October 2026 FGN bond auction result (16.79% FGN SEP 2036)
tbond_10y_rate.note: Marginal rate 17.29% on the 16.79% FGN September 2036 bond (9 years 10 months to maturity); the 2034 and 2038 bonds cleared at 16.99% and 17.19%.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Nigeria, corporate withholding taxes
tax_bank_interest.note: Interest paid to resident individuals and companies is subject to 10% withholding tax; the page does not say whether it is a final tax for individuals.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.sourceName: Debt Management Office, FGN Savings Bond offer for subscription, October 2026 (status of the bond)
tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: The offer states the bond qualifies as a government security under the Companies Income Tax Act and Personal Income Tax Act for tax exemption; individual holders are therefore treated as exempt. The offer still cites the pre-2026 acts, so confirm under the Nigeria Tax Act in force from 2026.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation, frequently asked questions (insured limits)
deposit_insurance_limit.note: Current insured limits: N5,000,000 per depositor in deposit money banks (including non-interest banks) and primary mortgage banks, N2,000,000 in microfinance banks; the same N5,000,000 applies per subscriber per bank under pass-through cover. The page is undated, so asOf is the research date.

credit_card_rate_cap.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026 (maximum lending rate)
credit_card_rate_cap.note: Average maximum lending rate of banks 32.62% in September 2026 (prime lending 19.04%); no card-specific cap or rate is published.

equity_return_low.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026; NGN per US dollar (CBN)
equity_return_low.note: Low case: Nigerian shares lag inflation, as they did in naira-weak years, returning about the after-tax deposit rate.

equity_return_base.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026; CBN treasury bill auctions (91-day 15.40%, 364-day 15.80% discount)
equity_return_base.note: Base case: about 2 points above the 14% inflation assumption and below the tax-exempt treasury bill yield (16-19%), well within the 4-point cap; the 10-year index record was not read and the market swings with the naira.

equity_return_high.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026
equity_return_high.note: High case: a strong decade for Nigerian shares in naira terms, as in 2023-2025.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria exchange rates (NGN per US dollar)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: flat dollar gold and slower naira depreciation.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria exchange rates; World Bank official exchange rate history
gold_return_base.note: Base case: the long-run dollar gold trend of about 4% a year plus about 9% a year of naira depreciation, roughly the gap between Nigerian and US inflation.

gold_return_high.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria exchange rates
gold_return_high.note: High case: strong gold years and a sharp naira devaluation.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026 (12-month deposit 10.50%)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: 12-month deposits at about 10.5% less 10% withholding tax.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026; DMO FGN Savings Bond offer, October 2026 (14.071%)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: a mix of term deposits (about 9.5% after tax), FGN Savings Bonds (13-14%) and treasury bills (16-19% yield).

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: CBN treasury bill auction of 28 October 2026; DMO October 2026 bond auction
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: treasury bills and FGN bonds at 16-17% less possible tax.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: NAICOM (the insurance regulator) publishes no industry-wide life claim settlement ratio that could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life and group life cover are sold, but no published premium rates per 1,000 naira of cover by age were found from NAICOM or another public source.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: No published typical cost of a major private hospital stay in Nigeria was found from an official or international source.

health_premium_table.note: No published private health insurance premiums by age per 100,000 naira of cover were found from NHIA or another public source.

oop_health_share.sourceName: World Bank WDI, out-of-pocket expenditure (% of current health expenditure), Nigeria
oop_health_share.note: 71.9% in 2023 (WHO Global Health Expenditure Database); older than 2025, the latest available.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: NBS CPI via Voice of Nigeria; inflation assumption 14%
goal_inflation_health.note: No national health CPI figure was read; imported drugs and equipment follow the naira, so 1.5 points above the 14% inflation assumption.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: NBS CPI via Voice of Nigeria; inflation assumption 14%
goal_inflation_education.note: No national education CPI figure was read; private school fees usually rise faster than general prices, so 1 point above the 14% inflation assumption.

life_expectancy.sourceName: World Bank WDI, life expectancy at birth, total (SP.DYN.LE00.IN), Nigeria
life_expectancy.note: 54.6 years in 2024 (men 54.3, women 54.9); UN WPP 2024 gives 55.0 for 2026.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via populationpyramid.net
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source of UN WPP 2024 medium variant for 2026; totals at 60, 70 and 80 are the mean of men and women (only the 65 total is published there).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: Working-age people per person aged 65+ = 100 / old-age dependency ratio: ratio 5.44 in 2025 (World Bank) gives 18.38; 6.0 in 2040 gives 16.67; 8.4 in 2065 (populationpyramid.net/nigeria/2065/) gives 11.9.

retirement_age_default.note: The Pension Reform Act 2014 (section 7) sets no retirement age: savings in the retirement savings account become payable on retirement under the terms of employment or at 50, whichever is later; employers set their own retirement ages.

retirement_age_government.note: The federal public service retirement age (commonly cited as 60, or 35 years of service) could not be read from an official text.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026 (12-month deposit 10.50%)
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: term deposits after the 10% withholding tax.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026; DMO FGN Savings Bond offer, October 2026
retirement_return_base.note: Base case: a mix of term deposits (about 9.5% after tax) and tax-exempt FGN Savings Bonds (13-14%), below the 1-year treasury bill yield (about 18.8%).

retirement_return_high.sourceName: CBN treasury bill auction of 28 October 2026
retirement_return_high.note: High case: most of the money in treasury bills and savings bonds.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Central Bank of Nigeria, money market indicators, September 2026
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case: a cautious mix earning about after-tax deposit and savings bond rates.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Debt Management Office, October 2026 FGN bond auction result; equity base 16%; gold base 13%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: a balanced mix of FGN bonds (about 17%), Nigerian equity funds and some gold, similar to a retirement savings account fund.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.sourceName: Debt Management Office, October 2026 FGN bond auction result; equity high 22%

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: No federal non-contributory old-age pension a person could claim was found in the sources read.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: No federal non-contributory old-age pension was found in the sources read.

gratuity_rule.note: No statutory gratuity or end-of-service rate for private employees was found: the Pension Reform Act 2014 only lets employers agree additional benefits on retirement (section 4(4)); the Labour Act text was not read.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: Pension Reform Act 2014 (National Pension Commission), sections 4, 7 and 10
public_pension_scheme.note: Contributory Pension Scheme for public and private employees: at least 10% of monthly emoluments from the employer and 8% from the employee into a retirement savings account; benefits (lump sum plus programmed withdrawal or annuity) on retirement or at 50, whichever is later. Contributions are tax-deductible and retirement benefits are not taxable. Benefits depend on fund returns, so not inflation-linked. Law from 2014 (older than 2025), still in force.

dps.note: No standard monthly recurring deposit product with a published rate was found.

sanchayapatra_5y.localNameEn: Federal Government of Nigeria Savings Bond
sanchayapatra_5y.note: Retail bond offered monthly by the Debt Management Office from N5,000 (maximum N50 million), in 2 and 3-year tenors with quarterly interest; sold through appointed distribution agents.

tbill_91d.note: 91, 182 and 364-day bills auctioned by the Central Bank of Nigeria; individuals buy through banks and brokers.

tbond_5y.note: Bonds of several maturities trade on the secondary market; 2026 auctions offered 2034-2038 maturities only.

tbond_10y.note: Auctioned monthly by the Debt Management Office (FGN SEP 2036 reopened in October 2026).

equity_fund.note: Registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission; equity and index funds invest on the Nigerian Exchange.

gold.note: Gold is mainly bought as jewellery; bullion bars and coins are uncommon for retail savers.

pensionScheme.name: Contributory Pension Scheme (National Pension Commission, PenCom)
